primary_source.citation: C. Davis and W. M. Kahan, The Rotation of Eigenvectors by a Perturbation. III, SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 7(1), 1970, 1–46.
primary_source.private_comparison_source: modernized local transcription; intentionally not distributed

status_definitions.compiled_exact: An exact source-facing theorem or construction is compiled on the base.
status_definitions.compiled_specialization: A useful compiled specialization exists, but not the full source scope.
status_definitions.compiled_general_infrastructure: The mathematics exists in a general reusable form, though a source-numbered wrapper may be absent.
status_definitions.candidate_under_repair: A statement/candidate exists in the full Part III repair campaign but is not compiler-certified on this base.

items.title: Two reducing decompositions and the residual
items.summary: Block decompositions for A and A+H, trial and exact coordinate maps, and R = (A+H)E0 - E0 A0.
items.notes: The exact notation is distributed across the Section 6 source data records rather than exposed as a Section 1 facade.
items.next_action: Add source-facing construction aliases only if useful for the full-paper facade.

items.title: Unitary-invariant norms and Fan dominance
items.summary: Norms determined by singular values, contraction laws, Ky Fan prefix norms, and dominance by all prefixes.
items.notes: The source norm correspondence is part of the clean Section 6 surface.
items.next_action: Retain as shared prerequisite; no new mathematics required.

items.title: Single-angle sine theorem
items.summary: Interval/exterior spectral separation gives delta times the directed sine norm bounded by the residual norm for every source unitary-invariant norm.
items.notes: The definitive source form is Theorem 6.1; real, complex, bounded, unbounded, and arbitrary-representative forms are present.
items.next_action: No mathematical gap. Keep the source audit synchronized.

items.title: Single-angle tangent theorem
items.summary: One-sided spectral separation plus the Rayleigh–Ritz/off-diagonal condition gives residual and perturbation tangent bounds in every unitary-invariant norm.
items.notes: The finite arbitrary-UI-norm theorem is compiled. General Hilbert-space and exact source wrappers are in the Part III repair campaign.
items.next_action: Certify the Hilbert-space source wrapper and exact perturbation companion.

items.title: Double-angle sine theorem
items.summary: A spectral gap between the two exact blocks yields residual and perturbation bounds for sin(2 Theta), with sharp factor two.
items.notes: Finite arbitrary-UI-norm forms are compiled; general Hilbert-space source forms are under repair.
items.next_action: Certify source-general residual and perturbation forms.

items.title: Double-angle tangent theorem
items.summary: Fully off-diagonal perturbations across an ordered gap give residual and perturbation tan(2 Theta) bounds with factor two.
items.notes: The finite operator-norm theorem is compiled. The source arbitrary-UI-norm Hilbert-space endpoint and branch selection are not yet certified.
items.next_action: Complete the general UI-norm source theorem and its selected acute branch.

items.title: Best constants and simultaneous equality
items.summary: All four constants are optimal in two dimensions, and finite direct sums realize equality simultaneously for all unitary-invariant norms.
items.notes: Sine sharpness and finite multiplicity are compiled; full quartet simultaneous equality remains in the Part III campaign.
items.next_action: Audit tangent and double-angle equality models against the exact source claim.

items.title: Unbounded self-adjoint scope
items.summary: The four theorem families extend to unbounded self-adjoint operators under bounded perturbation or residual assumptions, with analytic work concentrated in Theorem 5.2 and the Section 6 appendix.
items.notes: The sine family is complete in source scope. Other theorem families have partial unbounded APIs but no full source audit.
items.next_action: Track unbounded tangent and double-angle source coverage separately.

items.title: Direct rotation
items.summary: A unitary intertwining the two projections whose diagonal cosine blocks are positive and whose off-diagonal sine blocks are adjoints.
items.notes: Acute complex and finite constructions exist; exact nonacute source scope is not yet unified.
items.next_action: Add a source-facing definition covering the source existence regimes.

items.title: Acute case
items.summary: Both crossed intersections P ∩ Q-perp and P-perp ∩ Q vanish.
items.notes: The predicate is broadly used but lacks a numbered source alias.
items.next_action: Add a source alias only if the facade benefits.

items.title: Acute direct rotation existence and uniqueness
items.summary: In the acute case the direct rotation exists, is unique, and positivity of its diagonal blocks characterizes it.
items.notes: The main acute construction and uniqueness are present; the exact characterization by positivity needs source-level verification.
items.next_action: Prove or wrap the positivity characterization explicitly.

items.title: Nonacute existence criterion
items.summary: A direct rotation exists exactly when the two crossed intersections have equal dimension; it is then nonunique.
items.notes: No exact general Hilbert-space declaration was found.
items.next_action: State the cardinal/dimension-balanced existence theorem conservatively; finite and infinite cases may need separate APIs.

items.title: Principal square-root characterization
items.summary: Every direct rotation is a principal square root of the product of the two reflections; conversely a suitable principal square root is a direct rotation.
items.notes: The square identity and acute spectral branch exist; the source converse with the crossed-intersection mapping condition is not exposed.
items.next_action: Add the converse or record the exact missing nonacute hypothesis.

items.title: Square as a direct rotation
items.summary: When the cosine block squared is at least one half, U squared is the direct rotation from the reflected subspace to the target subspace.
items.notes: Square identities exist; exact source mapping between Q-minus and Q needs verification.
items.next_action: Add an exact source wrapper after the direct-rotation repair lands.

items.title: Classification of pairs of subspaces
items.summary: Spectral multiplicity functions of the two angle operators classify dimension-compatible subspace pairs up to isometric equivalence.
items.notes: The current angle API does not provide this full classification theorem.
items.next_action: Develop a two-projection canonical-decomposition classification, likely using Spectra/Halmos infrastructure.

items.title: Compact classification by angle eigenvalues
items.summary: When the cross projection is compact, the decreasing angle eigenvalue lists, including possible zero multiplicity, classify the pair.
items.notes: Depends on Theorem 3.1 plus compact spectral classification.
items.next_action: Defer until the general classification and compact spectral multiplicity bridge exist.

items.title: Angle commutation and eigenspace geometry
items.summary: The full angle commutes with both projections, the quarter-turn and direct rotation; its eigenspaces are maximal reducing constant-angle subspaces in the acute case.
items.notes: Commutation identities are present, but the maximal eigenspace characterization is not represented.
items.next_action: Separate the reusable commutation theorem from the source-specific maximality result.

items.title: Reversal symmetry
items.summary: Swapping P and Q leaves the angle operator unchanged and reverses the quarter-turn operator.
items.notes: Direct-rotation reversal is represented; the exact angle/J statement needs a source wrapper.
items.next_action: Add the source-facing angle and quarter-turn reversal theorem.

items.title: Pointwise and singular-value extremality of the direct rotation
items.summary: For any unitary carrying P to Q, an orthonormal sequence experiences angles at least the principal angles; equivalently the singular values of (1-V)|P are minimized by the direct rotation and equal 2 sin(theta_k/2).
items.notes: Only weaker/finite extremal endpoints are currently named; the full singular-value-by-singular-value source claim is not explicit.
items.next_action: State the weak-majorization or pointwise singular-value theorem that implies all norm corollaries.

items.title: UI-norm minimality of direct rotation displacement
items.summary: The direct rotation minimizes the norm of (1-V)P for every unitary-invariant norm.
items.notes: The current named theorem includes an angle restriction and may correspond more closely to Proposition 4.4.
items.next_action: Verify whether a general Corollary 4.1 endpoint exists; add it if the singular-value theorem is proved.

items.title: Basis-angle square-sum extremality
items.summary: For every orthonormal basis of P, the sum of squared displacement sines under V dominates the sum of squared principal sines.
items.notes: Finite candidate exists; infinite series/source scope requires audit.
items.next_action: Certify the finite proof and determine the exact infinite-dimensional summability convention.

items.title: Squared displacement UI-norm minimality
items.summary: The direct rotation minimizes the UI norm of (1-V*) (1-V).
items.notes: Finite candidate maps directly to the source formula.
items.next_action: Compile, promote, and add a source-numbered wrapper.

items.title: Real-space full displacement minimality below pi/3
items.summary: In a real Hilbert space, if the maximal angle is at most pi/3, the direct rotation minimizes every UI norm of 1-V.
items.notes: Finite candidate is present; source-general real Hilbert-space scope is not certified.
items.next_action: Audit the angle threshold, real scalar restriction, and infinite-dimensional norm domain.

items.title: Banach-space Sylvester lower bound
items.summary: Under a norm bound on B and an inverse norm bound on A, AX-XB=C implies ||C|| >= delta ||X|| for any compatible operator norm.
items.notes: The repository has Neumann and ordered-gap engines, but no explicit audited source wrapper for this Banach-space theorem.
items.next_action: Add the exact Banach-space statement and derive it from the geometric-series proof.

items.title: Semibounded self-adjoint Sylvester theorem
items.summary: For A >= gamma+delta > gamma >= B, a bounded solution of AX=XB+C satisfies the sharp UI-norm inequality.
items.notes: The completed Section 6 route contains the needed constant-one engines, while the exact source theorem alias is still in the full Part III repair campaign.
items.next_action: Expose an exact Theorem 5.2 wrapper and include it in the full-paper audit.

items.title: Strong-cutoff convergence of singular values
items.summary: If projections converge strongly to one, each singular value of K composed with the projection converges to the corresponding singular value of K.
items.notes: The modern approximation-number theorem is stronger and scalar-generic.
items.next_action: Add a source-numbered wrapper if needed by the full-paper facade.

items.title: Direct-sum UI-norm comparison and converse
items.summary: Two diagonal block inequalities imply the direct-sum inequality; under equisingularity of paired blocks the converse holds.
items.notes: Both directions are proved; the converse should be added to the exact audit manifest.
items.next_action: Harden the audit, not the mathematics.

items.title: Reflection-pinch contraction
items.summary: The sum of the two diagonal projection blocks of an operator is no larger than the operator in every source unitary-invariant norm.
items.notes: Part of the clean Section 6 surface.
items.next_action: No mathematical gap.

items.title: Symmetric sine theorem
items.summary: Two complementary source gap hypotheses give the full sine-angle inequality with perturbation H.
items.notes: Complex and real source forms are compiled.
items.next_action: No mathematical gap.

items.title: Generalized sine theorem
items.summary: A lower frame bound on the trial map and interval/exterior separation give delta epsilon times any equisingular sine representative bounded by the residual.
items.notes: This is the canonical source-general sine theorem.
items.next_action: No mathematical gap.

items.title: Pairwise-gap square-norm sine theorem
items.summary: Arbitrary pairwise spectral distance gives the sharp Hilbert–Schmidt/square-norm residual bound.
items.notes: The defect-first pairwise tensor proof is compiled.
items.next_action: No mathematical gap.

items.title: Generalized tangent theorem
items.summary: A strict-lower-rank trial space, Rayleigh–Ritz residual, and one-sided gap give the source UI-norm tangent bound.
items.notes: The finite arbitrary-UI-norm specialization is compiled; the source Hilbert-space theorem remains under Part III repair.
items.next_action: Certify the general Hilbert-space statement and exact dimension/cardinality formulation.

items.title: Unbounded-operator passage
items.summary: Domain invariance, bounded residual, spectral cutoffs, and limiting arguments extend the single-angle theorems to unbounded self-adjoint operators.
items.notes: The main common-domain and graph-core source forms are compiled.
items.next_action: Audit every displayed appendix identity, not only the headline theorem.

items.title: Finite-rank near-maximizer leakage estimate
items.summary: A nearly Ky-Fan-optimal finite-rank compression has small off-block trace norm.
items.notes: The surrounding approximation-number infrastructure exists, but no exact source declaration was found.
items.next_action: State and prove the source lemma; it may be useful independently for cutoff passages.

items.title: Reflection proof of the sine double-angle theorem
items.summary: Reflect the perturbation by 2P-1, identify U squared and sin(2 Theta), and reduce the result to the symmetric sine theorem.
items.notes: The reflection identities and finite theorem exist; the exact full proof package is under repair.
items.next_action: Add a source wrapper preserving both residual and perturbation conclusions.

items.title: Singular-vector proof of the tangent double-angle theorem
items.summary: The off-diagonal block equation and paired singular vectors yield Ky Fan and UI-norm bounds for tan(2 Theta).
items.notes: The operator-norm theorem is compiled in finite dimensions; the arbitrary UI-norm singular-vector argument remains uncertified.
items.next_action: Complete the exact source norm scope and infinite-dimensional approximation passage.

items.title: Branch selection and spectral repulsion
items.summary: Under tan(2 Theta) hypotheses, the acute branch is equivalent to the selected spectral ordering; a canonical reducing subspace exists and satisfies operator, eigenvalue, and symmetric-gauge repulsion inequalities.
items.notes: Several finite and continuation components exist, but all three source conclusions are not yet source-audited together.
items.next_action: Compile the continuation-selected branch and separate parts (i), (ii), and (iii) into explicit source declarations.

items.title: Smallness selects the acute branch
items.summary: If the perturbation or residual norm is below half the gap, the sine double-angle estimate is accompanied by Theta < pi/4.
items.notes: A priori angle bounds and continuation machinery exist; exact source hypotheses and both alternatives require audit.
items.next_action: Add the exact two-alternative source theorem.

items.title: Fourth-derivative Rayleigh–Ritz model
items.summary: The free-beam fourth derivative on L2(0,1), perturbed by multiplication by epsilon t, with the two-dimensional linear trial eigenspace.
items.notes: No source module formalizes the differential operator, boundary conditions, trial basis, or spectral gap alpha3 > 500.
items.next_action: Choose whether to formalize the analytic operator or a certified finite-data surrogate reproducing the paper computations.

items.title: Initial sine and sine-double-angle bounds
items.summary: Compute R*R and derive the operator- and two-singular-value bounds for sin Theta and sin(2 Theta).
items.notes: The general theorems exist, but the concrete residual matrix and numerical constants are not formalized.
items.next_action: Formalize exact radical inequalities first, with decimals as derived corollaries.

items.title: Rayleigh–Ritz tangent refinements
items.summary: Use the compressed trial operator and orthogonal residual to obtain sharper tan Theta and tan(2 Theta) bounds.
items.notes: Requires exact 2x2 matrix computations and application of Theorems 6.3 and the tan-double-angle theorem.
items.next_action: Build a finite-dimensional exact arithmetic model independent of the unbounded differential-operator construction.

items.title: Comparison with Weinberger bounds
items.summary: Derive lower-eigenvalue estimates from a 3x3 comparison matrix and compare individual-vector angle bounds.
items.notes: This imports an external theorem and asymptotic O(epsilon^4) discussion not currently distilled into Lean-ready statements.
items.next_action: Separate exact matrix eigenvalue inequalities from the historical comparison narrative.

items.title: Residual-infinite limitation example
items.summary: An l2 trial vector has a useful Rayleigh quotient but lies outside the perturbed operator domain, so residual-based theorems do not apply while lower-bound methods still do.
items.notes: This is an instructive domain counterexample and independently useful.
items.next_action: Formalize a corrected nearby domain example rather than the intentionally non-domain vector itself.

items.title: Individual eigenvector identification inside a cluster
items.summary: Reduce the full eigenproblem to a two-dimensional Schur complement, then combine tan(2 Theta) and tan Theta bounds to control each eigenvector angle omega_k.
items.notes: No current module represents the Schur-complement reduction or final constants.
items.next_action: Formalize as a standalone finite block-operator theorem, then instantiate the numerical data.

items.title: Sine bounds under arbitrary pairwise spectral distance
items.summary: Ask for the best UI-norm sine-angle estimate when the two relevant spectra are only known to be at distance delta.
items.notes: The paper resolves the square norm; the repository has the sharp pairwise Hilbert–Schmidt theorem. The all-UI-norm version remains a distinct question.
items.next_action: Record precisely which norm classes are resolved and which remain open.

items.title: Three-way subspace decompositions
items.summary: Seek perturbation estimates for two decompositions into three reducing subspaces using off-diagonal coordinate blocks.
items.notes: This is explicitly an open research direction, not a theorem required to formalize the 1970 paper.
items.next_action: Preserve as a documented research question; do not count as proof debt.

items.title: Joint eigenvalue–eigenvector bounds
items.summary: Seek optimal estimates coupling changes in eigenvalues and eigenvectors.
items.notes: Open research question.
items.next_action: Document only.

items.title: Perturbation bounds for functional calculus
items.summary: Seek bounds on f(A+H)-f(A) for broader functions, with spectral projections as the motivating discontinuous case.
items.notes: Open research question; modern operator-Lipschitz theory is outside the paper-completion target.
items.next_action: Document connections but do not treat as missing proof.
